findings.passage: Ensuring the integrity of our elections and returning that sense of trust that is the foundation of our government is by far my top priority in the new session.
findings.note: Swearing-in statement (House caucus site press release) naming election integrity as his top priority; no ID detail.

findings.passage: Citizens across the state have raised legitimate concerns about how the election was conducted, from the acceptance of late ballots to the use of drop boxes and lack of signature verification on mail-in ballots.
findings.note: Statement at the first State Government Committee election hearing; raises mail-ballot signature verification and drop boxes.

findings.passage: The Voting Rights Protection Act would tighten security by expanding upon Pennsylvania’s current voter identification law, require regular election audits, improve election uniformity among the 67 counties as required by the Pennsylvania Constitution, enhance certification processes for all machines used in elections, require signature verification using ballot scanning equipment for mail-in and absentee ballots, improve lists of registered voters and more.
findings.note: Press release in his name on his committee vote for HB 1300 (Voting Rights Protection Act). Describes the bill as expanding the voter ID law, adding mail-ballot signature checks and voter-list improvements, and giving voters a scannable registration card for in-person voting. Committee vote only; floor votes are linked separately.

findings.passage: I will be joining State Government Committee Chairman Seth Grove in working to advance a proposed constitutional amendment that will allow the voters to have their say on the issue of voter ID as soon as possible.
findings.note: Reacting to the governor's veto of HB 1300, he says he will work on a voter ID constitutional amendment.

findings.passage: The Voting Rights Protection Act would have addressed all of those by enhancing voter ID requirements, and providing an ID to ensure everyone could meet the requirement; expanding election audits; ensuring uniformity in the conduct of elections across counties; providing for early voting and correcting some defects on mail-in ballots; and offering counties more time to process registration applications and count ballots.
findings.note: Same release, describing HB 1300 as enhancing voter ID requirements with an ID provided to those who need one. It names him as a co-sponsor.
